title: Drum pedal and use of Derby mutes in the picture
summary: The men examine the crowfoot pedal and what is in the grass by Ory's foot, and Joseph says the only mute used then was the derby.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: How did that pedal work on that drum? I see they got no stand for the snare and then they got a pedal that looks like it goes sideways to me from the regular ones, huh?
That must be one of those crowfoot pedals. Yeah, that's what it was, yeah. Mmhmm.

Could I see it a second? Look and see what all they got in the grass. The microphone glass? Mmhmm. You can get it, Bill. They had a real good pedal in them times. See they got something in the grass right next to Ori and I can't see what it is.
Let's see. Here. Well I can't hold it. I'll hold the mic. You take that. Okay.
Can you see that, Bill? Right next to Ori and the grass right by his foot there. I can't see what that is.
Oh, yes. Just something holding that drum, that's all. Holding that drum on the sides, you know? Mmhmm. Just something holding that drum up. That's all? Yeah. Yeah. Sure.
Yeah, I thought maybe it was a mute or something he might have had. No, I know mute.
Did they use many mutes in those times? The only mute they used, they used Derby.
Well, they had, everybody had them, it looked like. The trumpet and the, the trumpet player and the trombone player, both.
Yeah. They used Derby. That was a mute. Mmhmm.
